Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority (EECA) (2010). Energy Efficiency Best Practice Guide: Steam Systems, Hot Water Systems and Process Heating Systems. Technical guide 8.0. EECA Business, Wellington, New Zealand (information current as of October 2010; adapted from a Sustainability Victoria publication).

Locators are printed page numbers (equal to PDF pages). A best-practice guide: almost all numbers are percentage savings reprinted from Carbon Trust (2004, 2006), ORNL (Harrell 2002) and US DOE (2004). Main file: hot water boiler lifetime 15 years; steam turbine with process exhaust overall efficiency almost 80%. _measures: Table 1 boiler savings, hot water steps, condensing boiler 10-20%, process heating savings. _other-values: lifetime cost split, NZ process heat statistics, steam leak and pipe-loss tables, Appendix D fuel heating values and NZD prices. Traps: the document is dated 2010 (copyright and disclaimer) though the file name says January 2011, so the id uses 2010; NZ energy statistics printed in TJ are likely PJ; no capital costs printed.
